evidence.quote: Be it enacted by the People of the State of Illinois

agora_harms: Violation of civil or human rights, including privacy

summary.short: Amends Illinois's civil remedies act for nonconsensual dissemination of private sexual images to cover intentionally digitally altered sexual images. Gives depicted individuals a civil cause of action against persons over 18 who disseminate such images without consent, with exceptions and damages remedies.
summary.long: Amends Sections 5, 10, 15 and 25 of the Illinois Civil Remedies for Nonconsensual Dissemination of Private Sexual Images Act. Sec. 5 defines terms including private, identifiable, child and sexual image. Sec. 10(a) gives a depicted individual a cause of action against a person over 18 who intentionally disseminates a private or intentionally digitally altered sexual image without consent, where the individual is identifiable, suffers harm, and the person knew or recklessly disregarded the lack of consent, the image's status, or identifiability. Sec. 10(b)-(c) provide that consent to creation or prior disclosure does not by itself establish consent, that disclosing alteration is no defense, and that interactive computer services are not liable for third-party content. Sec. 15 excepts good-faith disclosures by law enforcement, in legal proceedings, for medical education or treatment, or in reporting unlawful conduct or matters of public concern. A parent or guardian is not liable for a child's intimate image unless other law prohibits the disclosure or it was made for arousal, humiliation or gain. Sec. 25 allows a prevailing plaintiff to recover actual or statutory damages (up to $10,000 per defendant), monetary gain, punitive damages, fees and injunctive relief. Enforcement is by private action; no effective date is stated in the text.

evidence.provision: Section 5 (bill text, preamble to amended sections)
evidence.quote: The Civil Remedies for Nonconsensual Dissemination of Private Sexual Images Act is amended by changing Sections 5, 10, 15, and 25 as follows:

relations.note: Section 10(c) states that the Act does not impose liability on an interactive computer service, as defined in 47 U.S.C. 230(f)(2), for content provided by another person.

evidence.quote: Nothing in this Act shall be construed to impose liability on an interactive computer service, as defined in 47 U.S.C. 230(f)(2), for content provided by another person.

notes: The document shows the four amended sections in full with no underlining or brackets marking new text, so added and unchanged text cannot be separated. No effective date or enacting session law for this bill appears in the text. Each amended section carries the source note '(Source: P.A. 101-556, eff. 1-1-20.)', which names the prior enacting act; the bill is not linked to it in the text. Section 10(a) and (c) use 'intentionally digitally altered sexual image', which Section 5 does not define; Section 5(14) defines 'sexual image' to include images that 'falsely appear to show' a depicted individual. Sections 15(c)(1) and 25(c) refer to 'a law other than this Act' and 'any other law of this State' without naming any instrument.

thresholds.consequence: An individual under 18 is a child; the parent, guardian or custodian exception in Sec. 15(b) applies to dissemination of an intimate private sexual image of a child.
thresholds.conditions: Child must be unemancipated; exception in Sec. 15(b) is subject to Sec. 15(c).

evidence.quote: an unemancipated individual who is less than 18 years of age

thresholds.variable_text: age of defendant for civil action (person over 18)
thresholds.consequence: The civil cause of action under Sec. 10(a) lies only against a person over the age of 18 for intentional or threatened dissemination of a private or digitally altered sexual image.
thresholds.conditions: Also requires that the depicted individual suffers harm, is identifiable, did not consent, and that the defendant knew or recklessly disregarded the possibility of these facts.

evidence.quote: by a person over the age of 18

thresholds.variable_text: statutory damages per defendant (civil remedy cap)
thresholds.value_text: statutory damages, not to exceed $10,000, against each defendant found liable under this Act
thresholds.measurement: Per defendant found liable; covers all disseminations and threatened disseminations known or reasonably should have been known when the action is filed or that become known during the action. Court considers ages of parties, number and breadth of disseminations and other exacerbating or mitigating factors.
thresholds.consequence: Statutory damages available to a prevailing plaintiff as an alternative to actual damages are capped at $10,000 per defendant.
thresholds.conditions: Available under the 'greater of' election in Sec. 25(a)(1); other remedies under Sec. 25(a)(2) and (a)(3) are not subject to this figure.
